species: cat (Felis catus, isolated Pacinian corpuscle from mesentery) and frog (Rana temporaria, labyrinth)
readout_other: receptor and action-potential recordings from an isolated Pacinian corpuscle; evoked-potential recordings from the midbrain auditory area (torus semicircularis) in response to ultrasonic and sonic stimulation of the labyrinth.
direction_notes: Focused ultrasound excited isolated Pacinian corpuscles, producing graded receptor potentials and all-or-none action potentials, and excited mechanoreceptors in the frog labyrinth, producing midbrain evoked potentials similar in shape, amplitude and latency to those evoked by sound; responses disappeared after labyrinth destruction.

target.label: isolated Pacinian corpuscle with attached nerve fibre, from cat mesentery

timing.protocol_description: An isolated Pacinian corpuscle with its nerve fibre attached was placed in vaseline oil over the ultrasonic irradiator, in the centre of the focal region; ultrasonic stimuli were rectangular bursts with duration from 0.1 msec to hundreds of msec, and receptor/action potentials were recorded via cotton-thread electrodes moistened with physiological solution.

exposures.label: Frog's ear labyrinth, evoked potentials from contralateral midbrain auditory area

target.label: frog's ear labyrinth (inner ear), recorded from the contralateral midbrain auditory area (torus semicircularis)

timing.protocol_description: An immobilised frog (left labyrinth destroyed) was fixed over the irradiator so the focal region projected into the right labyrinth, with water as the coupling medium; potentials were recorded from the contralateral (left) torus semicircularis with a tungsten microelectrode and compared with responses to sonic tone stimuli of optimal frequency.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound stimulation was done by the use of an ultrasonic generator and focusing irradiator, the resonant frequency 0.48 MHz (for details, see ref. 4).
source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound stimulation was done by the use of an ultrasonic generator and focusing irradiator, the resonant frequency 0.48 MHz (for details, see ref. 4).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: At the left: response to a single stimulus 1 msec duration; to the right: responses to double stimuli, duration, 0.1 msec; interval, 3 msec.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.isppa_w_: The firing level for action potentials varied between 0.4 and 2.5 W/sq.cm.
source_quotes.exposures[1].timing.sonication_duration_: Thresholds for detectable responses, with stimulus duration of 1 msec, were in the range from 0.1 to 1.0 W/sq.cm, decreasing, with stimulus duration of 100 msec, to 0.01-0.1 W/sq.cm.
source_quotes.exposures[1].unspecified_domain.isppa_w_: Thresholds for detectable responses, with stimulus duration of 1 msec, were in the range from 0.1 to 1.0 W/sq.cm, decreasing, with stimulus duration of 100 msec, to 0.01-0.1 W/sq.cm.

flags.reason: Paper states burst durations ranged 'from 0.1 msec to hundreds msec' for both preparations; only the precise lower bound (0.1 ms) is recorded as a number, since 'hundreds' is not a specific value.

No target id in the taxonomy names the amphibian ear labyrinth specifically; 'vestibular_organ' is used as the closest anatomical match even though the structure is being tested here for its auditory (not vestibular) function.

Paper does not state the number of Pacinian-corpuscle preparations or frogs used in the main text (a figure caption implies at least 3 frogs, but figures are not used as a source of values); left not_reported.
